cases.name: built-in worked example
stdout: (demo: Example Co., fictional - 54 leads over four weeks; SLA settings are example inputs, not benchmarks)
AAJ - LEAD HANDOFF & SLA CHECK
THE HANDOFF IS LEAKING - 1 MQL never touched; 72% touched within 4 h against a 90% target; 3 MQLs waiting past the acceptance window; 2 leads scored as MQLs but never handed over.
54 leads, 36 MQLs, 36 due for a first touch (as of 2026-10-05 09:00)
RESPONSE TIME (target 4 h, calendar hours)
Touched within target (goal 90%): 72% (26 of 36; 90% range 59% to 83%)
Median time to first touch: 2.5 h across 35 touched MQLs
Slowest touched: L-34 at 2.6 days (1 lead)
Never touched, past target: 1 - L-46
Late or untouched leads that became MQLs outside Mon-Fri 9:00-17:00: 6
ACCEPTANCE AND CONVERSION
Sales accepted: 66% (21 of 32; 90% range 51% to 78%)
accepted 10 | converted 11 | rejected 11 | open 4
Decided within 2 days: 63% (20 of 32; 90% range 48% to 75%)
Open past the window: 3 - L-01, L-34, L-46
Rejection reasons: Wrong timing (5), No budget (2), Not a fit (2)
Accepted MQLs that converted: 52% (11 of 21; 90% range 35% to 69%) - directional, n < 30
THRESHOLD CHECK (MQL at 50; conversion of leads with a sales decision)
Under 50            19 leads   33% converted (1 of 3; 8%-75%) directional
50 to under 60      14 leads   10% converted (1 of 10; 2%-35%) directional
60 to under 70      11 leads   30% converted (3 of 10; 13%-56%) directional
70 and up           10 leads   67% converted (6 of 9; 40%-86%) directional

Conversion rises with score: 10% (1 of 10) for 50 to under 60 against 47% (9 of 19) for 60 and up. The 90% ranges overlap, so the data cannot yet say the threshold is too low. Leads under 50 that sales worked anyway converted at 33% (1 of 3), no worse than just above the line; also too few to read. Directional: at least one band rests on fewer than 30 decided leads (AAJ's rule of thumb).
36 MQLs = 9 a week against 9 promised - met on average; 1 of 4 full weeks fell short
THREE FIXES
1. Work the 1 MQL nobody has touched
L-46 became an MQL more than 4 h ago and has no sales touch. Give it a named owner today, then find where routing dropped it: no owner, no alert, or an alert nobody reads.
2. Lift response-time compliance from 72% to 90%

26 of 36 due MQLs were touched within 4 h. The slowest touched lead was L-34 at 2.6 days. Look at when the late leads arrived and who owned them before you change any scores. 6 of the 10 late or untouched leads became MQLs outside Monday-Friday 9:00-17:00; if your SLA counts business hours, some of these may be on time.
3. Get a decision on 3 MQLs waiting past the acceptance window (2 days)
L-01, L-34, L-46 have no accept-or-reject decision. An MQL in limbo is invisible to both teams: marketing thinks it was handed over, and sales has not said yes or no.
DATA NOTES
-  3 leads (L-08, L-11, L-17) became MQLs with a score below the threshold. Fine as a deliberate exception; a problem if it is routine.
!  2 leads (L-37, L-49) scored at or above the MQL threshold but were never marked as MQLs: a possible handoff leak.
!  2 leads (L-06, L-11) were rejected with no reason code, so nobody can learn from them.
Rules: rates on fewer than 30 leads are directional (AAJ's rule of thumb); ranges are 90% Wilson intervals; times are calendar hours.
